who: People working in a second language
takeaways: Timing is not an essential part of any activity, except non-interactive synchronized media, such as a video, and real-time events, such as a live auction.
It is Level AAA. At Level A, 2.2.1 allows time limits if people can turn them off, adjust or extend them. 2.2.3 asks for no time limits at all.
Unlike 2.2.1, there is no exception for limits that are essential. A timed quiz would fail.
It is worth meeting in learning, forms and anything people do at their own pace, where a timer adds pressure but no value.
failures: A training quiz with a timer on each question
A game level that must be finished before a countdown ends
An onboarding carousel that moves on before people have read it
check: List every timer in the product, visible or hidden, and what each one protects.
For each, ask whether it is a real-time event, a non-interactive video, or neither.
Remove or redesign every timer in the third group, and recheck the flow with no time pressure at all.

quiz.question: A compliance training course has a 30 second limit on each quiz question. The team wants to meet 2.2.3. What do you do?
options: Let people extend each question by another 30 seconds
Keep the limit, but show a visible countdown
Remove the limit and let people answer at their own pace
quiz.why: Extending would meet 2.2.1, and a countdown only makes the limit visible. Under 2.2.3 timing must not be part of the activity at all, and a training quiz is not a real-time event.

spec: List each time-based behavior and whether it is removed, user-controlled or an allowed exception.
For auto-advancing content, specify manual Next and Previous controls with no auto-advance.
Where a timer stays because the event is real-time, note why and what people see.
review: What is this timer protecting, and is it a real-time event?
Would the task lose anything if people had as long as they needed?
Are we keeping this limit because it is essential, or because it was always there?
tradeoff: Some products are built around time, such as games, timed tests and flash sales, and AAA cannot be met there without changing the product. Meet it in self-paced flows like learning and forms, and use 2.2.1 controls where time really is the point.
system: Make the default carousel, stepper and quiz components untimed, with auto-advance and timers as opt-in settings that need a reason.
pitch: A timer measures speed, not understanding. Removing it lets more people finish, and it costs us nothing.
